entertainment.body:
You could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang , the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia , the most important tech company in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy. The most valuable tech in the world — Huang’s super-powered computer chips — are smuggled into China or installed into data centers connected to America’s greatest rival. Above it all, the possibility of a super-intelligent AI , a true artificial mind, looms — and its creator will be positioned to rule the world.

At least, that’s the simple version of the story. But the real picture of the great geopolitical AI race is both more complex and more unbelievable than the tale of spies and smuggling that’s playing out in the press right now. China wants the U.S.’s chips — that much is clear. But why? And what can our only real rival power actually do with them? To answer this, Rolling Stone spoke with two experts in the Chinese tech sector, who pulled back the curtain on what the superpower actually wants when it comes to AI — and why it’s willing to use sex, smuggling and lies to get there.

Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, says Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.

The first is as a straight race to one goal: creating a truly intelligent AI that surpasses human intelligence in all general tasks and can improve itself autonomously. In the industry, this is known as AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence. This point of view holds that the first country or company to achieve true AGI will have an earth-shattering advantage over any competition in economics, war, medicine, and technology. Basically, it sets the world of AI up as a winner-take-all race. Many U.S. officials — including, at times, Trump himself — have made this argument, alongside many of the private sector CEOs actually working on the technology.

“If you start with that assumption, then the effort to slow down China is nearly existential,” Chan says. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

The biggest advantage the U.S. has is Nvidia’s chips. The most powerful computer chips in the world are made by one facility in Taiwan , using incredibly complex and rare machines manufactured by one company in the Netherlands. It is a process so detailed and scientifically complex that it might as well be magic. Other companies can make chips, of course, but none of them can make chips as well as the single manufacturing company in Taiwan that Nvidia and most of the U.S. tech giants use. AI companies need these chips, and these chips alone, to run the most advanced AI models — which is why the U.S. has done a lot to limit China’s access to them, setting export controls on who Nvidia can sell their chips to and which countries they can be shipped into.

entertainment.title: Gustavo Dudamel Enlists Dave Grohl, LL Cool J, Cynthia Erivo for Brad Pitt-Produced Documentary
entertainment.summary: The revered LA Phil conductor lets Rolling Ston e tag along as he closes one chapter and heads to New York for the next
entertainment.body:
I n December, Gustavo Dudamel will make his much-anticipated return to conduct the Los Angeles Philharmonic for a string of dates. It’s the first time he will head back to his former home of nearly 20 years since beginning his tenure as the New York Philharmonic’s Music and Artistic Director. Given the multiple standing ovations and chants of “Gustavo” that resonated through the Hollywood Bowl during his final LA Phil bow in late August, his arrival will be a much welcome one.

Alongside his trip back to the West Coast, Rolling Stone can exclusively announce a documentary about Dudamel and the LA Phil will premiere on Dec. 7 coinciding with his concerts at Walt Disney Hall on Dec. 4, 5, and 6. The documentary, titled Symphony of a Thousand , is described as “Set during challenging times in L.A., the film encapsulates Dudamel’s philosophy on how music can create connection and community in an increasingly fractured world.”

The Jennifer Tiexiera-directed film, produced by Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment, features footage from Dudamel and the LA Phil’s pair of performances at 2025’s Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, where they made history as the first major orchestra to perform a full set at the massive event. It features Dave Grohl, LL Cool J, Cynthia Erivo, Natasha Bedingfield, Becky G, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, and Zedd. Kevin Macdonald serves as the executive producer, with producers Jeremy Kleiner, Dede Gardner, and Chloe Mamelok.

Landmark pop culture moments like this have peppered the course of Dudamel’s trailblazing career. And he wasn’t about to go (east) quietly. His final nights helming the LA Phil culminated in a weekend at the Bowl that featured the Foo Fighters and other pop luminaries, concerts that doubled as a benefit for his home country of Venezuela. A conversation at the Grammy Museum followed.

“I met Gustavo at a party about 12 years ago, and I fell in love with him. As a heterosexual man, it confused me,” Coldplay ’s Chris Martin affectionately jokes when joining Dudamel and LA Phil onstage during the benefit concert for Venezuela finale. “And I realized it wasn’t so much sexual as musical in the way I just wanted to cuddle him forever. And we’ve been musically cuddling ever since.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

entertainment.title: TVLine's Performer Of The Week: Diane Morgan
entertainment.summary: Diane Morgan's Philomena Cunk explored film history with delightfully inane questions in Cunk on Cinema - here's why she's TVLine's Performer of the Week.
entertainment.body:

THE EPISODE | "A/Several Star(s) Is/Are Born " (November 15, 2026)

THE PERFORMANCE | There is no field of study that is safe from Philomena Cunk, it seems. After exploring world history in "Cunk on Earth" and the origins of existence in "Cunk on Life," the boldly oblivious investigative reporter played by Diane Morgan has turned her (admittedly spotty) attention to film with her new Netflix mockumentary "Cunk on Cinema." And Morgan was in fine form as she befuddled showbiz luminaries like Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch with Cunk's delightfully inane questions.

For the uninitiated, Philomena Cunk is a fictional character: a woefully uninformed reporter who tackles big topics by interviewing real-life experts and asking them incredibly stupid questions. "Cunk on Cinema" is broken up into six 15-minute episodes, and really, any of them would be a marvelous example of Morgan's peerless deadpan. But we'll focus on Episode 3, where she examined the rise of film stars like Marilyn Monroe and Marlon Brando — and asked Bay, "If you made a film that's 12 meters long at the cinema, would I need a 12-meter TV to watch it at home? Or do you just film it again with smaller actors and sets?" Morgan never cracked the slightest hint of a smile while Cunk doggedly pursued her wrongheaded lines of questioning, and part of the fun was seeing film historians left speechless at the stunning depths of her ignorance. And almost by accident, "Cunk on Cinema" actually became a pretty decent overview of film history, as Cunk's ridiculous inquiries eventually led us to the truth... if only by going in backwards.

"Cunk on Cinema" cements Morgan's Philomena Cunk as being right up there with Ricky Gervais' David Brent and Sacha Baron Cohen's Borat as one of this century's greatest British TV comedy creations. We can't wait to see what esteemed area of knowledge she'll mangle next. — Dave Nemetz

On the small screen, Kesy had a prominent role in all three seasons of Guillermo del Toro's FX horror series "The Strain," playing a monstrous vampire named Gabriel Bolivar. Following "The Strain," Kesy landed the part of mafia man Roller Husser in the raunchy TNT comedy "Claws". Kesy featured as Leon in the 2017 "Baywatch" film and he played the villainous mutant Black Tom Cassidy in 2018's "Deadpool 2". That same year, he returned to the world of gangsters when he portrayed The Fish in the Bruce Willis-led action flick "Death Wish". Kesy's filmography also includes the small part of U.S. Army Special Forces soldier Charles Jones in the war drama "12 Strong," as well as a black ops team member known as Thunder in the Tom Clancy military thriller "Without Remorse". In 2024, Kesy became the latest actor to embody the human-demon hybrid investigator Hellboy in "Hellboy: The Crooked Man".

Apple TV "12 12 12" starts off with a big heist, and Jack Kesy's Bobby Galvin is right in the middle of the chaos. Examining the event from three points in time, the premiere focuses on Bobby and his brother Paul (Jamie Dornan) robbing a bank vault in Zurich, Switzerland on Christmas Eve. It's an intricate operation that requires the duo to use an underground tunnel they drilled themselves and evade various security mechanisms.

Bobby isn't as sharp as his brother, and his recklessness clashes heavily with Paul's more methodical approach. From losing millions of dollars to committing acts of violence, Bobby can't seem to stay away from a life of crime, which interrupts Paul's plan to settle down with his girlfriend. Then there's FBI agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie), who relentlessly tracks the two and has a bit of a vendetta against them stemming from an earlier heist in Newark, New Jersey. The three main characters of "12 12 12" might be more similar than they appear on the surface, which makes each twist even more compelling.

entertainment.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Is All Over the Place (in a Good Way)
entertainment.summary: Featuring everyone from Travis Scott to Fuerza Regida to Michael McDonald, the soundtrack to the blockbuster video game is like a radio dial spinning on hyperspeed
entertainment.body:
The 13-years-in-the-making Grand Theft Auto VI has been hailed for its of-the-moment touches, but it does have one quaintly anachronistic aspect: Nobody reaches for the aux. The game’s in-universe radio stations provide the soundtrack to its criminal and romantic endeavors, with drivers eschewing streaming and flipping the dial until they find their favorites. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , appropriately, feels like a frantic flip through a dial so wide, it can even fit a still-trucking smooth jazz station.

Opening track “Starting From Zero,” a collaboration between the aggro-electro duo Justice (who composed the game’s score) and soul crooner Michael McDonald, transports the listener to the sublime, the combination of thudding synths and McDonald’s immediately identifiable voice throwing back to the days of hits being launched from buddy-cop movies and Miami Vice . It’s pastiche, sure, but it’s pastiche done well, and it bookends nicely with the album’s closing cut. “Overtown Lights,” a collaboration between Return to Forever bassist Stanley Clarke, pianist and bandleader Robert Glasper, and drummer Yussef Dayes, evokes a carefree late-night drive over streets slicked with rain and illuminated by reflected headlights.

If Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album were just a collection of homages to the good-ish old days of neon t-shirts paired with blazers, it would probably be a solid listen, as evidenced by the genre-splicing Justice-SZA-King Gizzard-Tame Impala team-up “Flower In A Hurricane” and the training-montage-ready Dua Lipa cut “Go Easy.” But this collection is more than that — similar to the game, whose intricate details firmly place it in a heightened version of the present, it’s a wide-ranging representation of popular music’s current moment. “That’s It,” the collaboration between Swedish MC Yung Lean, Atlanta kingpin Future, and superproducer Metro Boomin, follows the Justice/McDonald collab, and even though it opens with icy synths that feel connected to the previous track, the fluttering trap snares and bone-rattling bass, as well as Lean’s anxiety-ridden lyrics, jolt the milieu back to 2026. entertainment.title: Jason Scott and the High Heat Are the Cool, If Raunchy, Band Americana Music Needs
entertainment.summary: The Oklahoma City outfit serve up decadence in the video for "Shit Show" and blood in the clip for "How to Get Away With Murder," two tracks off their Play Boy album
entertainment.body:
“I write behind the wheel of the van,” Jason Scott, leader of the namesake band Jason Scott and the High Heat , says. “There’s no other time.”

Bassist Ryan Magnani, however, calls bullshit: The van is just one of the places that Scott, a prolific Oklahoma writer, is able to come up with material. “Just the other day, you came off of a drive and you said, ‘I think I just wrote a cool song.’ And I am looking around like, ‘Where did you write a song? You don’t have a guitar,’” Magnani says. ‘You said, ‘Nah, I was just thinking about it.’”

Jason Scott and the High Heat released their latest album Play Boy back in September, marking their second record on the Leo33 label and their second in just over a year, following the March 2025 drop of American Grin . Scott has spent the better part of a decade writing songs shaped by his Pentecostal upbringing and the personal and artistic awakenings he had after pursuing music full-time, but Play Boy goes hard in a different direction. It’s best described as “Jason Scott, unfiltered,” a collection of songs written on whims.

“It has no inherent meaning, and it did not come from anywhere,” Scott says, “other than, ‘That’s all we be doin’ out here.’”

With Scott on guitar and vocals and Magnani on bass, the High Heat features Gabriel Mor on guitar, Garrison Brown on guitar and keys, and Tremaine “Bobby” Wade on drums. Taylor Johnson, a one-time member, is the band’s producer. On this particular afternoon, they are gathered around a table at an Irish pub on Manhattan’s Upper West Side, coming in hot from a European run and gearing up for a CBS Saturday Morning taping the next day. Together, the High Heat are a group of misfits from Oklahoma capable of being sincere in one moment, and irreverent in the next.

The group skewed toward the latter when they introduced Play Boy to the world in early summer by releasing the twangy “Shit Show” and its accompanying video. Brett Loudermilk and Zain Curtis of Paperboy Studios, best-known for Ke$ha’s NSFW “ Boy Crazy ” video, oversaw the production, which opens with the band in a living room, nursing severe hangovers, before a parade of increasingly-absurd characters wanders in. entertainment.title: E.J. Carroll, ‘Boardwalk Empire’ and ‘Law & Order’ actor, dead at 66
entertainment.summary: The actor died suddenly Thursday while on his way to a voice-over booking, his representative, Jon Mason, revealed.
entertainment.body:
E.J. Carroll, best known for his appearances in “The Deuce,” “Boardwalk Empire” and the “Law & Order” franchise, has died . He was 66.

The actor died suddenly Thursday while on his way to a voice-over booking, his representative, Jon Mason, told Deadline on Friday .

“E.J. Carroll was a consummate actor known and loved for his intense commitment to the characters he played,” Mason told Deadline.

“There isn’t an actor in New York that hadn’t worked with or crossed paths with E.J., known for stealing scenes alongside Robert De Niro, Mickey Rourke, Bruce Dern and most recently Jalen Brunson and Quinta Brunson,” he added.

“He will be greatly missed by the acting community, which he lived for,” Mason concluded.

Mason also told People in a statement on Friday, “When E.J. Carroll performed, it was impossible to take your eyes off him. But his lasting legacy will be the kindness and generosity he showed his friends, fellow performers and even strangers.

Page Six has reached out to Carroll’s representative for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Born May 21, 1960, Carroll got his start with a 1998 appearance as a police officer on “Law & Order,” according to IMDb .

entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power Season 3: Who Is Landroval, The Prince Of Eagles?
entertainment.summary: Yes, it happened again: An eagle turned up to save the day in The Rings of Power. But just who is Landroval, and what's his role in the history of Middle-earth?
entertainment.body:
Prime Video Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 4.

A lot happens in "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 4. Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) is finally reunited with her husband, Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower), and at the end of the episode, we meet Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin) in his new Nazgnagôl garb. Theo subsequently kills Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) in a powerful moment that marks the cliffhanger for the season's first half.

In the midst of all the guts and glory, a Great Eagle arrives and bears Galadriel and Celeborn to safety. As this winged hero arrives, Galadriel names him as "Landroval, Prince of Eagles." It's a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment in a busy sequence, but it's also an intentional line — one that connects the two elves' airborne savior to one of the most important birds in Middle-earth history.

In "The Return of the King," Landroval is named as the brother of Gwaihir the Windlord. Tolkien describes the two brothers as the "greatest of all the Eagles of the North, mightiest of the descendants of old Thorondor, who built his eyries in the inaccessible peaks of the Encircling Mountains when Middle-earth was young."

Prime Video The Great Eagles are a famous and recurring part of Tolkien's storytelling. We first meet them in "The Hobbit," in which their unnamed leader is referred to as the "Lord of the Eagles." They also play an ongoing role in "The Silmarillion" and "The Lord of the Rings," most often as the messengers of the Valar, the god-like guardians of Middle-earth, in their interactions with Men, Elves, and others.

Tolkien's thoughts about what the Great Eagles were varied over time. We know that some of them, like Landroval, continue to show up over millennia of storytelling, so they're clearly not ordinary birds. What isn't clear is whether Tolkien ever conclusively decided if they were merely talking beasts or more powerful beings, like the angelic Maiar. "The Silmarillion" leans toward the latter explanation; that book describes the lofty abode of Manwë, the King of the Valar — who's associated with wind, air, and birds — like so: "Spirits in the shape of hawks and eagles flew ever to and from his halls; and their eyes could see to the depths of the seas, and pierce the hidden caverns beneath the world."

In the First Age of Middle-earth, the Great Eagles show up often, including Gwaihir, Landroval, and their dad, Thorondor. In the Second Age, the Eagles are less busy, but they do play a key role in the eventual fate of Númenor. And yes, as you may have guessed, this makes Landroval's appearance in "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 4 something of a creative liberty on the part of the showrunners.

entertainment.title: How Robert Pattinson shed his ‘Twilight’ heartthrob image to become the quirkiest James Bond yet
entertainment.summary: "Twilight" director Catherine Hardwicke told Page Six that she recognized Pattinson's star potential in his very first audition when he was 21 in 2007.
entertainment.body:
The next James Bond is just like his signature martini — dry, with a twist.

On Monday, it was announced that Robert Pattinson will be the new 007 . While the 40-year-old has already starred in three blockbuster movie franchises — “Harry Potter,” “Twilight” and “The Batman” — he brings a deadpan, eccentric personality to mainstream Hollywood hits.

“Twilight” director Catherine Hardwicke recognized Pattinson’s star potential in his very first audition when he was 21 in 2007, exclusively telling Page Six that it was because of his quirky disposition — not in spite of it — that he nailed the lead as the sexy, brooding vampire, Edward Cullen.

“He certainly can be [suave], but he also is just funny and hilarious and offbeat and very original,” Hardwicke said, revealing that she always knew Pattinson had the acting chops for a franchise like “James Bond.”

“He’s so elegant in a way, even though he’s quirky and fun and mischievous and all, but he’s just got that body that looks great in a tux,” she laughed.

In fact, Hardwicke believes Pattinson’s eccentricity is precisely what makes him the perfect fit to play the iconic tuxedo-clad spy.

“It just adds to the richness of a character and feel that’s coming through in his performances. There’s a lot more underneath the surface,” she said.

A Hollywood source echoed that sentiment, telling Page Six that Pattinson is “definitely quirky” but “super talented” and will “elevate” the Bond brand.

entertainment.title: Never Lend Money, Pay Your F-cking Taxes, and More Life Advice From Leslie Jones
entertainment.summary: The comedian, SNL vet, and host of HGTV’s Roast My Rental looks back on lessons learned over decades in entertainment
entertainment.body:
T here’s not a room in the world that could fit all of the trinkets, gifts, and prized possessions comedian Leslie Jones has accumulated through her career.

“I always keep something,” Jones says on Zoom from her Los Angeles home, panning the camera to show a wall of white shelves packed to the brim with tchotchkes. But it’s hard for her to pick favorites — especially since they all have treasured memories that go along with them. “Colin [Jost] gave me a trophy that said ‘Baddest Bitch in the World,’” she says with a laugh, pointing at the memento. “I’ve still got that one.”

Jones might be one of the best-known late-bloomers in show business. In 2014, she joined Saturday Night Live as a writer before being promoted to a featured player. She was 47 at the time, making her the oldest person ever to join the cast. But even with two decades of stand-up work under her belt, slogging through bombed sets, late-night performances, and side hustles, Jones says she doesn’t regret her winding path to comedy fame. In fact, she’s adamant that if success had happened for her any sooner, she wouldn’t be here to talking to us. “I would have been a cautionary tale,” she says, plainly. “I would have made all the wrong decisions.”

Jones spent five seasons on SNL , where she established herself as a comedic voice known for taking wild — and often foul-mouthed — swings at everything from dating during slavery to abortion bans to plans for her own funeral. This brash self-assuredness followed her even after her tenure, as she expanded her résumé to include TV and film roles in projects like Ghostbuster s and Coming 2 America as well as professional fan duties — Chief Super Fan Commentator, to be precise — for NBC’s Olympics broadcasts. From her New York Times -bestselling memoir Leslie Fcking Jones to her latest gig hosting HGTV’s Roast My Rental (which debuted over the summer and re-airs through the end of November, and can be streamed on HBO Max), Jones has cemented herself as an outspoken and hilarious presence in pretty much any medium. entertainment.body:
ABC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The 1980s was a pivotal time for TV comedy, with several sitcoms coming to define the decade. The likes of "Cheers" and "The Golden Girls" were huge at the time, and their legacies live on to this day. However, for every sitcom smash hit, there were at least twice as many flops.

These failures include derivative rip-offs, misguided TV adaptations of popular movies, and, for some reason, an obsession with primates. Some of these shows should have been hits based on the talent involved, but mediocre execution and lack of audience engagement led to ruthless cancellations.

From a bizarre science fiction sitcom that was widely mocked at the time to a hilarious satirical sitcom that was just too ahead of its time to be appreciated, we've ranked the five biggest sitcom flops of the 1980s from least to most infamous.

NBC In 1987, Diane Keaton starred in the film "Baby Boom," written by Nancy Meyers and directed by her then-husband Charles Shyer. It follows a career-focused yuppie suddenly tasked with raising her cousin's child. NBC was keen to turn the successful film into a sitcom, and they hired Meyers and Shyer for the job. However, Keaton did not return for the series and was instead replaced by "Charlie's Angels" star Kate Jackson. The show debuted in 1988, and it quickly became clear that it wasn't going to last.

At the insistence of Meyers and Shyer, who wanted the show to resemble their movie, "Baby Boom" didn't have a laugh track. This was an unusual choice for a sitcom, and it seemingly put viewers off. The situational humor also didn't translate the way it did in the film. What's more, according to Shyer, he and Meyers weren't on the same page as Jackson, and at one point the star actually quit the series outright. The network eventually got Jackson back on board, but Meyers and Shyer soon called it quits themselves. 13 episodes were made, but only 10 made it to air.

CBS/YouTube While there are plenty of examples of great TV shows based on movies , "Stir Crazy" is not one of them. The 1980 film "Stir Crazy" stars Gene Wilder and Richard Pryor as two friends who get framed for a bank robbery and sent to prison. Directed by the great Sidney Poitier, the movie was a box office hit. In 1985, CBS attempted to capitalize on the success of that film with a comedy series of the same name. The show featured Larry Riley and Joseph Guzaldo as the two friends who are wrongfully convicted, but it failed to entertain viewers.

entertainment.title: Kate Middleton makes emotional cancer confession in trailer for secretly filmed documentary
entertainment.summary: "Cancer does change you," she admitted in the preview, released ahead of the film's Nov. 30 premiere on NBC.
entertainment.body:
Kate Middleton is opening up about how her cancer battle changed her forever.

The Princess of Wales made an emotional confession about the lasting impact of her diagnosis in the trailer for her secretly filmed documentary, “Heal,” which dropped Saturday .

“Cancer does change you,” she admitted in the moving preview, released ahead of the film’s Nov. 30 premiere on NBC. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

The surprise documentary follows Middleton as she takes on the grueling National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

The 44-year-old royal completed the challenge in late June to support The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, while reflecting on her own health struggles and connecting with others affected by serious illness.

“Healing is a journey,” Middleton said in the trailer. “How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”

The footage also captures a particularly poignant exchange between the princess and her younger brother, James Middleton, who accompanied her for portions of the climb.

“Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?” James asked, referring to the tradition of celebrating the end of cancer treatment.

entertainment.summary: The actress exclusively spoke to Page Six in New York City earlier this week ahead of the Season 35 finale, airing Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on ABC and Disney+.
entertainment.body:
Julia Stiles admits it was tough getting cut from Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars.”

“I definitely poured my heart and soul into it,” the actress exclusively told Page Six at the Cinema Society screening of “Unbearable Christmas” in New York City earlier this week.

“I got a lot out of it, no regrets, totally worth it. But it is hard to be doing something so intensely and then have it stop all of a sudden.”

Stiles competed alongside pro dancer Ezra Sosa and was eliminated during “Disney Night.”

Some of their most memorable routines together included a heartfelt tribute to the actress’ late “10 Things I Hate About You” co-star, Heath Ledger, during “Dedication Night,” a nod to her signature “Save the Last Dance” moves during “Super Bowl Night” and an energetic Quickstep honoring Dolly Parton (who died earlier this year) during the Season 35 premiere.

Despite being booted from the hit dance competition series, Stiles and Sosa grew super close and even got matching tattoos to commemorate their bond.

Stiles told Page Six that getting to dance with Sosa — and exercise that much throughout the competition! — was “wonderful,” and kept her “so present.”

“Besides my rib injury [I suffered], my body felt great,” the 45-year-old actress said. “I ended up doing things that I never thought I’d be able to. Like all the lifts and tricks, I never thought in a million years that I’d be able to do that.”

entertainment.title: Why The Number 47 Appears So Often In Star Trek
entertainment.summary: What started off as an in-joke for a writer has spiralled into an Easter Egg for fans that still pops up. We take a look at what "47" means to Star Trek.
entertainment.body:
Paramount Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It all began in Claremont, California, when Professor Donald Bentley made a playful mathematical proof that every number is equal to 47. This statistical joke snowballed into a new and unofficial school tradition created in 1964, where students would try to document the number 47 in the wild. Fast forward to 1990, when Pomona College alum Joe Menosky joined "Star Trek: The Next Generation" in Season 4 as an executive story editor, with Season 4, Episode 6, "Legacy," being his first credited episode.

As a graduate of Pomona's class of 1979, Menosky decided to incorporate his school tradition into the sci-fi series as an Easter egg for those who knew the lore. In Volume 41 of the Pomona College Magazine, Menosky discusses his reasoning for the 47 references: "It seemed like placing 47s [in the show] rather than just spotting them would be a way to continue the reference for any alumni who happened to watch the series." These references transformed from fan service for Pomona alumni and students into a running joke within the writers' room, as other writers also decided to sneak the number into their scripts.

Paramount/YouTube Writer Brannon Braga credited Joe Menosky ( via cudebi ) with beginning the tradition among the writers, revealing that it was picked up by him, Jeri Taylor, and Ronald D. Moore (creator of "Battlestar Galactica" ). Braga also recalled how he put the number throughout, in both the dialogue and visual scenes. However, the joke's novelty wore off eventually. Moore disclosed in an AOL chat that Menosky was the originator of the gag, but the references were gradually being phased out: "They've been cut down as we've kinda tired of this particular inside joke."

There are many nods to the number 47 in the franchise. A Code 47 is an encrypted message meant only for captains and senior officers. In Season 3, Episode 20, it is confirmed that the Ghorusda incident led to 47 casualties. Season 4, Episode 19 has Data reveal that the Enterprise's shields only had 47 seconds before they failed. Whether it is explicitly through dialogue or hidden subtly in background displays, 47 has become an important part of the lore despite being relatively inconsequential. The number still appears in later series, such as in "Star Trek: Discovery" Season 3 and "Star Trek: Lower Decks."

entertainment.title: Why Mariska Hargitay Considered Quitting Law & Order: SVU - And What Stopped Her
entertainment.summary: Plenty of major actors have left "Law & Order: SVU" before, but the show nearly lost its most notable actress after 27 seasons of leading the show.
entertainment.body:
Virginia Sherwood/NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit" wouldn't be what it is if it weren't for Captain Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) policing the streets of New York. Yet, there was a time that the cop drama almost lost its leading lady. After her fellow co-star Chris Meloni (aka Detective Elliot Stabler) departed "Law & Order: SVU" in 2011, Hargitay became the sole protagonist of the series and wasn't able to expand her horizons as a performer. She considered walking away from "Law & Order: SVU" during Season 25 to pursue other opportunities within different genres. Despite showing her comedic chops during her short-lived role in "Seinfeld," the actor rarely got to step out of her iconic character and display her sense of humor.

In a conversation with Julianna Margulies ( who previously quit "ER" in Season 6 ), Hargitay said she had thought of leaving the Dick Wolf procedural but admitted she wasn't ready to say goodbye. "Because I loved it," she explained in an interview with Variety . "And then I got to do all this other stuff, and that's why I don't think about leaving right now." Hargitay did get the chance to branch out without having to let go of the badge, though. She directed a 2025 documentary titled "My Mom Jayne", where she revisited her late mother's legacy. It won two Emmys, and it even helped lead to NBC choosing Hargitay to host the 2026 awards ceremony. The actor also made her Broadway debut with "Every Brilliant Thing," a solo play that is both hilarious and life-affirming. Hargitay played a nameless protagonist who chronicles every brilliant thing in the world to cheer up those around her and herself.

His most recent appearance was tied to a conviction from one of their earlier cases. The duo is forced to consider whether the person they arrested was indeed guilty of raping and murdering a young nun. As they head upstate and interrogate people who knew the victim, Benson and Stabler have a long discussion about their shared history and ponder the mistakes they've made while handling this case.

Fazekas told The Hollywood Reporter that she sought to make "an old school Benson and Stabler episode" to commemorate the show's milestone. Although fans have been rooting for the characters to get together, the showrunner believes that the episode's final moments show that both of them still have a lot of work to do before taking that next step in their relationship. "Is there time down the line? Maybe, but I think he's got some work to do. She can have some work to do as well, but I think she's probably a little further down that path than he is," she told The Hollywood Reporter.

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Judi Dench: 'Ask Me What I Did Yesterday And I Couldn't Tell You, But...'
entertainment.summary: Famous for Shakespeare plays and 007 movies, Judi Dench has a unique perspective on childhood memories now that she's more than 90 years old.
entertainment.body:
Denis Makarenko/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Judi Dench is a generational talent who has routinely graced the stage and screen since her professional debut in 1957. Dench starred in a string of Shakespearean plays like "Hamlet" and "Macbeth" in these early years, establishing herself as a notable theater actor for the National Theatre Company and the Royal Shakespeare Company, before branching into film and television.

Dench, of course, gained mainstream popularity after playing M in "GoldenEye," a role she reprised in eight more "James Bond" films. The actor won an Academy Award for her role in "Shakespeare in Love." She has also starred in "Chocolat," "The Chronicles of Riddick," "Pride & Prejudice" (2005), "Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides," and "The Second Best Exotic Marigold Hotel."

Other prominent projects include "Mrs. Brown," "Notes on a Scandal," and "Belfast." Dench also appeared in Kenneth Branagh's 1996 adaptation of Shakespeare's "Hamlet." She has earned a Tony, and two Golden Globes, along with several BAFTAs and Olivier Awards.

Dench brings robust expertise and exceptional talent to both stage and screen, which is why she is today's quote of the day.

Static Media "Ask me what I did yesterday and I couldn't tell you, but I can recount in vivid detail what I did over 80 years ago — the holidays, the friendships and the mischief I got up to at school."

The above quote is from Dench's 2026 interview with People . On the topic of childhood remembrance, Dench said that she is "amazed" at how much she remembers from that time. While comparatively recent events often escape her mind, Dench is able to vividly look back at her childhood and feel the warmth shared with friends.

Speaking about her childhood, Dench recalled her troublemaking ways. "My God, I was a real tearaway — setting off fire extinguishers and tying my fellow classmates to their chairs. I'm surprised I wasn't expelled," the actor mused. There's genuine fondness in the way Dench looks back on her mischief-laden school years, and how they remind her of a simpler time.

Dench also shared her early ambition to become a ballerina, and how she eventually became invested in acting on the stage. "My earliest ambition was to become a ballerina, but when my father pointed out I'd have to retire by the time I was 40, I decided it probably wasn't for me," Dench added.

Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin Herbert was a pro bowler last season, but he’s having a rough year in 2026, with career-worst numbers in almost every category. In his first six seasons, he averaged 27 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions per year. However, over halfway through the 2026 season, he has thrown for just six touchdown passes and already has 11 interceptions. He didn’t have a very productive game as a passer against the Ravens on Monday night, but at least he managed not to throw an interception for the first time all year as the Chargers finally won their first game to improve to 1-8. He also rushed for a season-high 51 yards and a touchdown. DJ Uiagalelei is the backup but he’s completed just two NFL passes in his career. They have five offensive linemen on injured reserve, including well known names like Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins. Pipkins was activated for practice last week, though, so his return is possible on Sunday. His official game status is questionable. Unsurprisingly, this has led to the Chargers struggling to protect Herbert, who has been sacked 33 times. Only Deshaun Watson has been sacked more often that that this season. The only two players to start every game so far have been second round rookie Jake Slaughter at center and veteran right guard Cole Strange. At the moment, Joe Alt is at left tackle, with sixth round rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Slater and Penning had started off the year on the left side, but Alt moved across from right tackle and Taylor stepped in when each of them got hurt. sports.title: Jerry Jones on fan's death after fight at 49ers-Cowboys game: "We had no record of an incident"
sports.summary: This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium.
sports.body:
On Friday, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about the incident during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

“ I just got that information , and so we had no record of of an incident, and we’ll be obviously looking into that,” Jones said. “My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn’t feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren’t aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game.”

They know about it now, and they have the resources to fully investigate.

“We really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago,” Jones said. “We have quite a surveillance of what’s going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn’t know of any incident. We’ve got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day.”

Jones said he’ll pass along any surveillance footage the Cowboys have to investigators.

A full and complete investigation could potentially create liability for the venue. It all depends on the facts. And, frankly, it requires the authorities not to sit and wait for whatever is voluntarily provided but to use the subpoena power to go get anything and everything that will allow the complicated puzzle to be put together as to what happened to Marco Narro, whether it could have or should been prevented, and whether the aftermath could have or should have been handled differently.

sports.title: Daiyan Henley being out with a knee injury changes nothing about the failed trade to Broncos
sports.summary: The failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returned to the front burner on Friday, with the news that Henley will miss Sunday's game against the Jets due to a knee injury.
sports.body:
It was a knee condition that prompted the Broncos to pull the plug on the deal — after trying to renegotiate the terms after the trade deadline.

From Mike Klis of 9News, who covers the Broncos: “Chargers ILB Daiyan Henley missed entire week of practices with knee injury and has been ruled out for game vs Jets. This validates concerns raised by Broncos medical team and GM George Paton. And proves Chargers were not on the up and up .”

Does it really prove that the Chargers weren’t “on the up and up”? The issue is that the Denver physical flagged a knee problem. In lieu of finding that the physical had been failed and that the trade won’t happen, the Broncos were willing to give Henley a passing grade, if the compensation was changed.

Henley has played every game this season. He played on Monday night against the Ravens. As far as anyone knows, he injured the knee during that game.

As far as anyone knows, the currently injured knee isn’t the same knee that created the concern during the Denver physical.

It’s all just noise at this point. The core problem is the ability of a team — after the trade deadline has passed — to renegotiate the terms of a trade. And the related issue is the ability of a team to give a conditional grade on the pass-fail question of a physical that is tied to the specific compensation.

A player either passes the physical, or he fails it. The process shouldn’t include an epilogue premised on the outcome of the physical being “maybe.” Especially after the time for negotiating trades has ended.

sports.title: Raiders owner Mark Davis hated the Madden movie
sports.summary: Did anyone read the script before allowing the Raiders' name and logo to be used?
sports.body:
The Raiders owner teed off on the Madden movie , in an interview with John Katsolimetes of the Las Vegas Review-Journal .

“My comment is, it’s full of turducken,” Davis said initially.

“It depends on whether you like turducken or not, and obviously, I don’t like turducken,” Davis said.

“I think it’s really it’s unfair to take people that have passed away and make caricatures out of them, and try to sell it as truth,” Davis said. “They start the movie with a statement saying that all of it’s not true, but some of it is, so it’s confusing what to believe.”

That’s not an uncommon device. “Based on a true story” means that plenty of liberties will be taken in an effort to make the story more compelling.

Mark Davis had one specific concern regarding the shading of the truth. He objected to his father’s reaction to the serious neck injury suffered by Patriots receiver Darryl Stingley, during a preseason game in 1978.

“So John goes over to the hospital afterwards, you know, and really looks after him,” Mark Davis said, “and there’s a scene where my dad is telling John, ‘You don’t need to go over there. You don’t need to take care of other teams’ players. You take care of our players.’

“That’s just so far from the truth. Anybody who has ever known him knows my dad always took care of people behind the scenes. If it was a player from another team had an issue that wasn’t being taken care of, my dad would quietly take care of that even if it was players on other teams. I’m serious. . . . It just it felt cheap to me to build up John’s image at the expense of my father’s.”

sports.title: NFL didn't know Puka Nacua had surgery when agreeing to suspension
sports.summary: The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions.
sports.body:
After Rams coach Sean McVay disclosed to reporters that Nacua had surgery to repair a torn MCL suffered during a Week 9 win over the Commanders, Judy Battista of NFL Network reported this: “The NFL did not know Puka Nacua had had knee surgery on Tuesday when it suspended him yesterday.”

Surely, that’s accurate; Judy is a solid reporter. But that extra fact doesn’t matter to the NFL’s ultimate handling of Nacua.

The report creates the impression that, during the negotiations that resulted in the three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua and/or his representatives withheld material information. That, at some level, the league had been duped by the lack of knowledge that Nacua had undergone surgery that will sideline him for “a couple months.”

First, the suspension (as the league affirmatively explained on Thursday) is separate from the injury. The NFL listed multiple examples of players who served suspensions while injured.

Second, whether Nacua (who had already missed one of the four minimum games he’s required to miss while on IR), was already going to serve the entirety of the suspension while on injured reserve with or without surgery.

Third, the surgery and the extended absence actually avoids the possibility that Nacua would have returned to action exactly one game after finishing his suspension, resulting in no net games missed due to the suspension.

The mere existence of the report represents an implicit acknowledgement by the league that the negotiated suspension, aimed at allowing Nacua to double-dip when it comes to his stint on injured reserve and his suspension, underscores the broader question of whether players should be allowed to serve a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy when otherwise unable to play. That’s a separate issue for the NFL to revisit, if it chooses, through a potential revision to the terms of the policy.

As explained on Friday, the league could have refused the deal. It could have insisted on pushing the issue through the full process, with Judge Sue L. Robinson conducting a hearing and the outcome potentially being appealed (by Nacua and/or the league) to the Commissioner. But that would have entailed a non-zero-percent chance that Nacua wouldn’t have been suspended at all.

Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won’t like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows.

The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium . Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in “the region,” not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city.

The Eagles’ lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.

sports.title: Jaguars saw something in Liam Coen that other teams didn't
sports.summary: The Jaguars identified Coen as their No. 1 candidate and re-shaped their front office to get him, at a time when other teams weren't even interviewing him.
sports.body:
Coen’s great success should have other teams that hired new head coaches in 2025 asking themselves: What did we miss? Because the Jaguars were so high on Coen that he was their No. 1 target and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him, while no other team even bothered to give Coen an interview.

During the 2025 NFL coaching search , we tracked dozens of reports of head coaching interviews and requests among the seven teams that had vacancies. The Jaguars were the only team that so much as asked Coen to interview.

This week there’s been some media scrutiny on the Jets, who hired Aaron Glenn without considering Coen as a candidate. Glenn is 5-22; Coen is 20-6. But it’s unfair to single out the Jets for failing to interview Coen, because no team other than the Jaguars did, either.

The 41-year-old Coen had a résumé that should have made him a good candidate. NFL teams area always on the lookout for coaches who can nurture a franchise quarterback and run an innovative offense. Coen played quarterback at UMass and coached quarterbacks in college before getting hired by Sean McVay to work on the Rams’ staff, eventually became the Rams’ offensive coordinator under McVay, and had been a successful playcaller as offensive coordinator for the Buccaneers, as well as at Kentucky. With that background, it’s surprising that only the Jaguars wanted him.

And the Jaguars really wanted him, to the point that they were willing to do whatever it took to hire him. Coen initially turned the Jaguars down and agreed to a contract extension to stay with the Buccaneers, but Jaguars owner Shad Khan wouldn’t take no for an answer. When Coen said he was concerned about the direction of the Jaguars’ front office, Khan fired General Manager Trent Baalke and agreed to reshape the front office in a way that Coen would approve of if Coen would take the job. Coen was persuaded to take the Jaguars job, and the Jaguars later hired James Gladstone, who had worked with Coen on the Rams, as GM.

The result has been the Jaguars going from one of the worst teams in the NFL to one of the best. Coen’s success in Jacksonville has justified the faith Khan had in him. And raises questions about the total lack of interest from the rest of the league.

sports.title: Nicolas Cage on his John Madden misfire: "I'm not Frank Caliendo"
sports.summary: This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.
sports.body:
That’s the one line that resonates most strongly in the new Madden movie. Because it’s exactly what John Madden would say if he saw it.

It’s bad. It’s very bad. Anyone who says it’s good has no taste and/or an agenda that involves the strategic application of lips to asses.

The biggest problem is Nicolas Cage as John Madden. Anyone who vividly remembers the unique charisma of John Madden knows instantly that nothing about Cage’s portrayal reflects the true nature, spirit, and demeanor of one of the most important and impactful figures in the entire history of the sport of football.

Cage, who seems to realize that his portrayal missed not only the bull’s-eye but also the entire wall on which the dart board was mounted, has defended the outcome by peering down his nose at the sports world.

“ He was not on my radar ,” Cage said of Madden, via Kirsten Chuba of the Hollywood Reporter . “I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever.”

“I’m someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation,” Cage explained regarding the decision to attempt to play the towering, iconic figure. “It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me.”

The audience has learned that Cage’s interpretation is nothing like Madden.

“That’s what acting’s about,” Cage said. “I’m not an impressionist, I’m not Frank Caliendo. I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I’m trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation.”

sports.title: Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers
sports.summary: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.
sports.body:
The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent.

That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary.

Once he clears waivers, however, he’ll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won’t be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he’s been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary.

Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings’ practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

sports.title: NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games
sports.summary: After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audienc
sports.body:
Via The Athletic , the NFL will consider adopting a minimum-night stay for teams playing internationally.

“Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.”

The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual “Opening Night” media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities.

“Having access to players and that type of experience when they’re in the market does have a lasting impact,” O’Reilly said. “That’s a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you’d want a club in the market for more than the day before.”

Beyond impacting strategic considerations, it would add to the total expense. The money would be worth it, if it further enhances the league’s overall reason for going global.

sports.body: The New York Jets are, embarrassingly, a three-point underdog on Sunday against a team who didn’t earn their first win until less than a week ago. The Los Angeles Chargers will be looking to build on their 23-20 win over the Ravens, and the Jets are making the long trip out west to take them on. Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to inject some positivity into their season: Playing the slots Last week, we discussed the Jets’ varying options for their slot cornerback position and they eventually went with one of our suggestions, which was to primarily use Minkah Fitzpatrick there in nickel packages, bringing Malachi Moore off the bench to fill in at safety. The Jets potentially face a similar dilemma in the slot this week, albeit on offense. Both Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams have been unable to practice, so if neither can go on Sunday, the Jets will have to make a change. One option could be to go with the guys currently on the roster. You could reactivate Jelani Woods and Tim Patrick and either run more multiple tight end packages, or use players like Garrett Wilson there. Another option could be to bring up Sterling Shepard or Jamaal Pritchett from the practice squad. The job share at running back remains a work in progress The Jets are still trying to figure out how to get the best out of Braelon Allen and Breece Hall now that both are healthy at the same time. Allen’s performances while Hall was out proved that he can benefit from a bigger workload. However, Hall brings different things to the table in the passing game, so the Jets will want him on the field more often than not. Last week was interesting because they employed Hall more in the passing game in the first half with Allen getting more carries. At the half, Allen had six carries and Hall had just two. However, after halftime, Allen carried the ball just twice and Hall had nine carries. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. The Chargers’ run defense did a great job against the Ravens, holding them to 16

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. sports.body: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football. Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced that they will retire wide receiver Andre Reed’s No. 83 jersey at some point during the 2027 NFL season. While the team did not announce when it will happen, they did announce that it will happen, giving fans the news that the retirement ceremony will happen sometime during next season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2123567003025784832?a=eiDWs2sPcy4ZrR46DXg&s=20] Reed is Buffalo’s franchise leader in targets (1,585), receptions (941), receiving yards (13,095), and receiving touchdowns (86). He played in Buffalo for 15 seasons, earning seven consecutive Pro Bowl nods from 1988-1994. He was named Second-Team All-Pro by the Associated Press in 1989 and 1990. A fourth-round draft choice out of Kutztown State University in Kutztown, PA, Reed was a key piece of a Buffalo team that made 10 playoff appearances, five AFC Championship Game appearances, and four Super Bowl appearances during his time with the franchise. At the time of his retirement, Reed ranked No. 3 all-time in receptions, and while he has since slipped to No. 23 all-time, it doesn’t dampen his accomplishments at all. A more pass-happy game has replaced the style of football played during Reed’s time in the league, making his numbers that much more impressive. Currently, Reed’s No. 83 jersey is worn by tight end Keleki Latu. Based on this announcement, it appears that Latu will need a new jersey number next year. Congratulations to Andre Reed—Go Bills!
